title: scheduler-refactor-kernel-mismatch-long-tail-investigation
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: After the scheduler refactor shipped in runtime-1.20, several clusters reported a reproducible increase in p95/p99 token latency for mixed-workload queues. This ticket drives the investigation, short-term mitigations, and medium-term hardening to prevent recurrence.

Timeline:
- 2025-10-28: Scheduler refactor merged (PR #4128). Change adjusted kernel scoring to prefer lower-initial-latency kernels for short sequences.
- 2025-11-01: We started seeing sporadic p95 increases on multi-customer shared pools during peak traffic.
- 2025-11-02: Incident declared; initial rollback for a small canary region performed.

Findings:
- Root cause: the new scoring heuristic undervalued throughput consistency for mid-length sequences (128-512 tokens). Under mixed batch composition the scheduler started routing subsets of requests to a kernel variant that had lower single-request latency but worse batching behavior. That mismatch led to inefficient batch formation, KV-cache pressure, and amplifier tail-latency when batches missed the expected coalescing window.
- Contributing factors: (1) Dynamic probing frequency increased after refactor, causing transient oscillation; (2) No guardrail to prevent kernel probing during sustained high-concurrency; (3) Insufficient synthetic tests for mixed-length batching patterns.

Impact: Medium customer impact across multiple shared pools, increased cost due to reduced token throughput and manual mitigation work. No data loss or customer-visible errors reported, only higher latencies and occasional timeouts for strict SLO routes.

Scope of work in this ticket:
- Capture full artifact set (logs, flamegraphs, perf counters) and correlate with request-length histogram.
- Implement emergency mitigations (circuit breaker + conservative fallback) and deploy canary.
- Add deterministic selection fallback for SLA-critical routes.
- Create regressions tests that emulate mixed-length batch behavior and KV-cache warmups.
- Instrument new metrics and Grafana dashboards to track kernel oscillation score/decision rate and batch coalescing efficiency.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 and p99 on affected pools return to baselines within 1 week of mitigation in canary and 95% of production pools within 3 weeks.
- Automated test harness introduces at least two synthetic scenarios that previously triggered the regression and are run in CI gating scheduler changes.
- New Grafana panels and alert rules for kernel-oscillation-rate and batch-formation-efficiency are live and documented.
comments: 2025-11-02 - Jonah Patel: Initial investigation shows kernel-selection decisions correlate with sudden drops in batch sizes. Pulling perf traces for region-us-west-2.

2025-11-03 - Aisha Raman: Deployed an emergency canary that forces deterministic kernel for routes with >90th percentile token length. Canary shows p95 drop ~30% in affected queue (dashboard link below).
2025-11-05 - SRE (Marta Li): Observed oscillation window of ~12s where kernel probing triggered repeated cache evictions. Propose reducing probe frequency and adding backoff amplification.
2025-11-07 - Eng Review (Prakash Iyer): Agreed on two-step mitigation: (1) disable probing under sustained concurrency, (2) introduce a conservative scoring multiplier for throughput. Preparing PRs.
2025-11-12 - Jonah Patel: PRs opened: PR #4362 (probe-backoff), PR #4370 (deterministic-fallback). Load test results attached. Moving to canary rollout for PR #4362.
2025-11-18 - Aisha Raman: Canary for probe-backoff shows stable kernel-selection entropy and batch-formation metric improvement. We still need synthetic CI tests and dashboard alerts before closing.
proposed_actions: Emergency: deploy probe-backoff and deterministic fallback to canary regions (PR #4362, PR #4370).
Short-term: revert the scoring weight change for mid-length preference and re-evaluate with mixed-length simulator.
Medium-term: add CI regression tests that replay multi-tenant traffic profiles across 1k+ synthetic users (task: create runner and test vectors).
Long-term: introduce an entitlement-aware kernel policy layer that pins SLA routes to deterministic kernels and exposes tuning knobs in Redwood Console.
Observability: add Grafana panels and alerts: kernel_oscillation_rate, batch_coalescing_efficiency, kernel_probe_fail_rate.
